validity.recommendation: Keep P0293 and P0147 as SEPARATE rows - do not merge. Record the mutual-exclusivity relationship (only one of the two will ever be built, ~80% shared alignment) in ResearcherNotes / AltPipelineNetworkGrouping so totals are not double-counted.
validity.researcher_notes: IDENTITY / DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION - the headline question for this row. Conclusion: ASAP (P0293) is NOT a duplicate of Alaska LNG (P0147), and it has NOT been folded into AKLNG's Phase 1. It is also distinct from P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project and P0174 Denali. Evidence: (1) SPONSOR'S OWN WORDS - AGDC senior VP Frank Richards, quoted by Oil & Gas Journal and KTUU in June 2018: 'AGDC is advancing two [Alaska North Slope] gas pipeline projects on parallel paths but only one will be built'; the two 'share a common mainline alignment for more than 80% of the route' but AKLNG adds liquefaction and export. Mutual exclusivity plus a shared corridor is a redundancy relationship, not one project entered twice. (2) SEPARATE REGULATORY TRACKS - ASAP is permitted by the US Army Corps of Engineers under CWA s404 / RHA s10 (NOIs 2009 and 2014, Final SEIS 22 Jun 2018) and holds Alaska DNR right-of-way lease ADL 418997; AKLNG is a FERC project. Two dockets, two lead agencies, two sets of permits. (3) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL PROJECTS - ASAP: 737 mi, 36-inch mainline + 12-inch/29-30 mi Fairbanks lateral, 1,480 psig, 500 MMcf/d, in-state delivery into ENSTAR at Point MacKenzie. AKLNG's pipeline: 42-inch, ~3,500 MMcf/d, to a Nikiski liquefaction plant. Same corridor, different pipe. (4) STILL SEPARATE TODAY - AGDC's ASAP page (current): 'the corporation is primarily focused on the Alaska LNG Project. ASAP remains as the State's back up project'; AGDC's FY2026 Capital AFE (June 2025): ASAP 'was idled following the completion of major permitting and is not currently active', while Phase 1 FEED work proceeds under the AKLNG banner. ASAP was left dormant as the state's fallback, not absorbed. (5) Against P0146/P0174: those are the 2008-2012 Alaska Gasline Inducement Act-era EXPORT trunk proposals to Alberta by TransCanada/ExxonMobil and BP/ConocoPhillips respectively - different sponsors, different destinations, both cancelled; the P0146 shard already adjudicated those two as genuinely competing proposals rather than one project. No DUPLICATE flag is raised. The caveat is bookkeeping only: any Alaska North Slope capacity/length total that adds P0293 and P0147 together is double-counting a corridor that can only be built once.

validity.researcher_notes: ShelvedYear = 2021 has no event behind it. The only thing 2021 corresponds to is EIA's bookkeeping: EIA's ASAP rows first show Status 'On Hold' in the 2021-07 release, carrying 'Last Updated Date' 2021-04-09 - that is the date EIA re-coded its own status field, not a date anything happened to the project. AGDC's own FY2026 Capital AFE (June 2025) confirms the causal link - ASAP 'was idled following the completion of major permitting'. Major federal permitting formally closed with the joint USACE/BLM Record of Decision in March 2019, which is why 2019 is a defensible alternative; I could not reach a citable primary URL for that ROD (the Anchorage Press write-up now soft-404s, poa.usace.army.mil returns 403 and the BLM ASAP plan page 404s), so the sourced proposal is 2018, the year the owner said it on the record. Searched: Federal Register full text (16 'Alaska Stand Alone' documents, 2009-2021), Alaska DNR/SPCO's ASAP record and ADL 418997 public notices, all 28 EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects releases 2018-05 to 2026-08, AGDC's publications and Alaska news coverage 2018-2026.

cross_row_leads.facts: Oil & Gas Journal, 25 Jun 2018, quoting AGDC: the Alaska LNG Project and ASAP 'share a common mainline alignment for more than 80% of the route', both are buried pipelines supplying Alaskans, but Alaska LNG 'includes a liquefaction and export component to ship ANS gas to buyers across the Asia-Pacific region'. AGDC SVP Frank Richards: 'AGDC is advancing two [ANS] gas pipeline projects on parallel paths but only one will be built.' AGDC joined the Alaska LNG Project in 2014 and assumed control of it three years later (2017). Relevant to P0147 as the sponsor-dated statement that AKLNG and ASAP are mutually exclusive, not the same project - do NOT merge the two rows.

AGDC's current ASAP page states AGDC is 'primarily focused on the Alaska LNG Project' and that 'ASAP remains as the State's back up project' - i.e. as of 2026 AKLNG is the active project and ASAP the dormant alternative. Useful for P0147's status review: AKLNG is the one AGDC is advancing.

AGDC FY2026 Capital AFE (18 Jun 2025) separates the two: 'AGDC was originally formed to develop the Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline (ASAP) Project in 2010. The ASAP Project was idled following the completion of major permitting and is not currently active' - while the AFE's capital request covers the Alaska LNG Project work. Confirms for P0147 that Phase 1 does NOT subsume ASAP.

USACE Notice of Intent, 74 FR 63736 (4 Dec 2009), for the State of Alaska's ASAP: alternatives explicitly include 'two pre-build options, using a proposed Alaska-Canada Gasline as the transport to the takeoff points'. Confirms that the Alaska Gasline Inducement Act-era Alaska-to-Canada trunk (P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project / P0174 Denali) was a SEPARATE, contemporaneous project that ASAP treated as an external alternative - supporting the existing P0146/P0174 boundary rather than any merge with P0293.

summary: ASAP (AGDC, 737 mi, 500 MMcf/d, shelved) confirmed real, correctly classified and NOT a duplicate of P0147 Alaska LNG despite an ~80% shared corridor - AGDC says only one of the two will be built and ASAP sits idled on its USACE/Alaska DNR permits; two spec concerns staged: ShelvedYear 2021 (an EIA bookkeeping date) should be 2018, and StartYear1 2025 is a lapsed target EIA itself withdrew.
